data.title: Skeleton of "Split the bill": Vite, TypeScript and make check

events.goal: Take the four split-bill tasks through the process completely on your own, without me
requirements: Take the tasks one by one: statement → code → review → checks → commit
Start each next task again with the statement from the analyst
I approve the statement in advance — do not wait for me
To the analyst's questions, choose a simple, reliable option that is clear to the user, and write the decision into the statement
On the third return do not stop: decide on your own — simplify or cut what does not work, but without bypassing the checks — and note it in the final report
Do not bypass or disable the checks
Commit each task with your own commits and push
Do not delete anything outside the task and do not rewrite git history
Task 1: make the skeleton of the web app "Split the bill" on Vite, TypeScript (strict), Vitest, ESLint and Prettier
Add the target make check (types, linter, tests, build), put it into verification.commands, and src into verification.paths, then run npx cyberzavod sync
Make the page: participants, expenses (who paid, how much, for whom) and the summary — who owes whom how much
Task 2: settle the debts with the minimal number of transfers, with tests for the edge cases: one paid for everyone, mutual debts, kopecks and rounding, zero expenses
Explain the calculation clearly in the interface
Task 3: make the "Share" link — the whole state of the bill is encoded in the page address, without a server, and the link opens the same bill
A broken or old link must not break the page — show a clear message
Task 4: lay out the page for a phone from 360 px and write the README: what it is, a screenshot or GIF, how to run it
Add a GitHub Actions workflow for deployment to GitHub Pages; I will turn Pages on in the settings myself — write in the README and in the report what to click
When all the tasks are ready, run /publish-recording: I approve the draft and the tables in advance — check them yourself by the rules of the skill and publish one recording per task
Commit the recordings, push, open a PR into main and merge it
In the final report, for each task write what was done, how many returns there were and which decisions you made without me, list the published recordings and what I need to do by hand

events.line: Accepted, I will study the code and write the statement of task 1
events.text:
Write the statement of task 1 from the series for the split-bill project. There is no code in the repository yet, only the project rules and the harness settings.

Task: the skeleton of the web app "Split the bill" on Vite, TypeScript (strict), Vitest, ESLint and Prettier. The target make check (types, linter, tests, build) must become part of the project checks, the check paths are src, after that the sync must be run. On the page: participants, expenses (who paid, how much, for whom) and the summary — who owes whom how much.

The summary must work already now, a simple correct calculation is enough: amounts in kopecks as integers, the domain logic separate from the interface and with tests. Minimizing the transfers, the "Share" link, the mobile layout and the README are the next tasks, but the skeleton must not get in their way.

The human's decisions are made in advance: the statement is approved, resolve the forks yourself and put them into the section "Accepted decisions"; no UI framework unless there is a weighty reason; the currency is rubles; put the formatting command into the project rules; do not edit generated files by hand; make check must be fast and work without a network after the dependencies are installed, the lock file is committed. Follow the project rules: interface texts and comments in Russian, identifiers in English.

events.line: Here is the statement: tools, logic, three sections
events.text:
The statement is ready. Goal: a skeleton appears on Vite, TypeScript (strict), Vitest, ESLint and Prettier with the target make check, and on the page "Split the bill" the user adds participants and expenses and immediately sees who transfers how much to whom.

Tools: package.json with the scripts dev, build, preview, typecheck, lint, test and format; a strict tsconfig; a flat ESLint config that forbids the domain logic to touch the DOM and the interface; Prettier with default settings; a Makefile where make check runs types, linter, tests and build in turn through the package.json scripts and without npx.

The domain logic is pure functions without the DOM. Money: amounts in kopecks as integers, rubles are parsed with string operations without float and shown through Intl. The bill: participants and expenses, adding and removing without changing the source data, a name check (empty, duplicate ignoring case) and a check whether a person takes part in the expenses. The calculation: dividing an amount into shares with the remainder by the kopeck to the first recipients, participant balances and a simple greedy calculation of transfers. Minimization will be done by task 2: it will replace only the transfers file.

The interface is vanilla TypeScript and the DOM, one section each for participants, expenses and the summary. The only mutable variable is the current bill, the forms are built once, only the lists and the summary are redrawn, user text is output only through textContent. The texts of errors and hints are given in the statement, the summary lies in an aria-live area.

The project rules and the harness settings: in the rules the lines about formatting and checks are updated, in the check settings — make check and the path src, then the sync.

Done criteria: make check passes without a network after the dependencies are installed and takes under a minute; the sync repeated changes nothing; formatting does not touch generated files; the linter fails if the logic touches document or the interface; the scenario "Ann pays 900 for three" gives two transfers of 300 rubles; 100 rubles for three are divided into 34, 33 and 33 kopecks; a name with markup is shown literally; all input errors show the needed texts, and the bill does not change. Every module has tests next to the code.

Accepted decisions: no UI framework; jsdom only for the DOM test; prettier is not part of make check; a participant who is in the expenses cannot be removed; names are unique ignoring case; the line of checks in the project rules is edited by hand because the sync does not touch it. Out of scope: minimizing the transfers and explaining the calculation, the "Share" link, the mobile layout, the README and deployment.

events.line: Accepted. I make the skeleton by the statement, then make check
events.text:
Do task 1 of the split-bill project by the approved statement. There is no code in the repository yet. Do not commit — the lead will do it. First read the project rules: names from the domain, no magic values, immutability, one function — one action, nesting no deeper than two, texts and comments in Russian, identifiers in English.

The content of the statement: a skeleton on Vite, TypeScript (strict), Vitest, ESLint and Prettier; the target make check made of types, linter, tests and build; domain logic without the DOM (money, bill, shares, balances, greedy calculation of transfers); a vanilla interface of three sections — participants, expenses, summary; the texts of errors and hints, the done criteria and the list of tests are given in the statement; the project rules and the check settings are updated, then the sync is run.

The lead's correction: when trying to remove a participant who is in the expenses, the message is this — "Can't remove {name}: there are expenses with this participant. Remove them first".

At the end run the formatting and make check, it must be green, and check that a repeated sync changes nothing. In the answer write what was done by the points of the plan, what deviations there were and why, and the result of the checks.

events.line: Here you are. The skeleton is ready, make check is green, 71 tests
events.text:
Task 1 is done, nothing is committed. After the dependencies are installed, make check is green in about 8 seconds: types, linter, 71 tests in six files and the build.

Done by the plan: tools (package.json with a lock file, a strict tsconfig, an ESLint config forbidding the DOM in the domain logic, Prettier, a Makefile without npx, an extended ignore list); domain logic (money, bill, dividing into shares with the remainder to the first, balances, greedy calculation of transfers); interface (the page, three sections, shared helpers, texts as in the plan, including the correction about removing a participant); the project rules and the check settings, the sync is done, make check is listed in the generated file. The tests lie next to the code, the DOM test covers the scenarios from the criteria about the summary, markup in a name and input errors.

Deviations from the plan: a function that gets a participant name by id is added, because the name is needed both in the expenses and in the summary; a file with the shared section interfaces is added; error messages are reset on any redraw of a section; the change of the participant list in the expenses section is detected by the change of the list reference; in the balance calculation there is a fallback value of zero because of the strict index check.

Checks: formatting and make check are green; after formatting the generated files do not change; a repeated sync changes nothing; temporary files that break the rules broke the linter on both rules and were removed. The scenario in the browser was not run by hand, only by the DOM test.

events.line: Accepted. I will go through the 11 criteria and the deviations
events.text:
Review the uncommitted changes in the repository for task 1: the skeleton of "Split the bill" on Vite, TypeScript (strict), Vitest, ESLint and Prettier with the target make check and a page of participants, expenses and a summary. The harness settings file and the generated rules file do not need to be checked by content, it is enough to make sure that it was updated by the sync and not by hand.

The done criteria are these. make check passes without a network after the dependencies are installed and takes under a minute, any error gives a non-zero exit code. The check settings equal make check and the path src, the sync repeated changes nothing. The project rules state the formatting and the checks. Formatting does not touch the generated files. The linter does not go into service directories and fails if the logic touches document or the interface. strict and the index check are enabled in tsconfig. A lock file exists. The scenario "Ann pays 900 for three" gives two transfers of 300 rubles, after the expense is removed the hint comes back. 100 rubles for three are divided into 34, 33 and 33 kopecks. A name with markup is shown as text. Five input errors show the given texts, and the bill does not change.

Assess whether the deviations from the executor's report are justified: the function that gets a participant name, the shared section interfaces, the reset of messages on redraw, detecting the change of participants by reference and the fallback value in the balance calculation. The project rules — readability, names, immutability, nesting, no magic values, texts in Russian. You may run make check and the linter. Do not change files.

events.line: Accepted: 11 criteria are met, small remarks do not block
events.text:
ACCEPTED. All 11 done criteria are met. There are no serious remarks, only small ones, and none of them blocks the task.

The criteria were checked in a separate copy: after the dependencies are installed, make check runs in turn and takes about 8.5 seconds, 71 tests are green; a type error and a linter violation give a non-zero exit code. The check settings are right, a repeated sync changes nothing, the generated rules file is reproduced without changes. Formatting touches nothing, the linter does not go into service directories and catches both document and imports from the interface. The scenarios about the summary, markup in a name, input errors and dividing kopecks are covered by tests. The lock file has only the official package registry, there are no secrets.

All deviations from the plan are justified: the name function is needed in two places and fails when the participant is missing; the shared section interfaces have three real implementations; the reset of messages is appropriate because a redraw happens only after a successful change; the change of participants by reference works and is confirmed by a test; the fallback value in the balances is unreachable and does not hide an error.

Small remarks: in the expenses section a nested call inside a conditional expression should be moved to a variable; the function that builds the expenses section is long and mixes levels; the globals ban does not catch access through globalThis; the order of functions in the bill file makes it hard to read from top to bottom; one constant is exported without need; two test functions that read messages can be merged.

My failure: the first attempt to make a copy failed, so part of the commands ran in the main copy. Temporary files appeared there and were removed, the state matches the original, further checks went in the copy.

events.line: Accepted. I will check the criteria and run the scenario in the browser
events.text:
Check task 1 of the split-bill project against the done criteria. The changes are not committed, they lie in the working copy. Test rules: tests next to the code, DOM tests with the jsdom environment mark, a test checks behavior.

Task: the skeleton "Split the bill" on Vite, TypeScript (strict), Vitest, ESLint and Prettier with the target make check; a page with participants, expenses and a summary by the greedy calculation, minimization is the next task. The criteria are the same as in the review: make check passes without a network and takes under a minute; the check settings and a repeated sync; the project rules; formatting does not touch generated files; the linter fails on access to document and on an import from the interface; a strict tsconfig; a lock file; the scenario "Ann pays 900 for three" gives two transfers of 300 rubles; dividing 100 rubles into 34, 33 and 33 kopecks; markup in a name is shown as text; five input errors with exact texts.

Experiments that break the code or the settings do in a copy of the repository in a temporary directory, not in the main working copy. In the main one change only tests. Run the scenario in the browser through the build, the preview and Playwright from a temporary directory, without adding dependencies to the project; Chromium is preinstalled. If it does not work out, write what remained unchecked.

events.line: Checks passed: all 11 criteria, in the browser too
events.text:
CHECKS PASSED. I did not add or change tests, the experiments went in a copy of the repository, I did not edit the main copy.

make check passes in about 8 seconds: types, linter, 71 tests and the build. In the copy a type error and a substituted expectation in a test give a non-zero exit code, installing dependencies without a network worked in three seconds. The check settings are right, the sync result does not change. The project rules state the formatting and the checks. After formatting there are no changes in a clean tree. Access to document and an import from the interface fail the linter; broken files in service directories it does not notice, as intended. The needed flags are enabled in tsconfig, the lock file exists.

The scenario is confirmed by the DOM test and in the browser: I built the project, started the preview and ran the scenario through Playwright. After the expenses the result was "Ben → Ann: 300,00 ₽" and "Clara → Ann: 300,00 ₽", after the expense was removed the hint "Add expenses — here it will appear who owes whom how much" appeared. Dividing 100 rubles into 34, 33 and 33 kopecks, markup in a name as text and five input errors are confirmed by tests.

What remained unchecked: disabling the network while installing dependencies, and whether make check takes under a minute with a cold cache: the measured 8 seconds were on a warm machine.
